clue.text: Rook finished attack

parts.note: something finished is over, done with
to charge is to attack, rushing at an enemy

explanation.surface: In a chess game, a rook has completed an assault on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the chess piece, but here it is the verb meaning to swindle a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat them, especially by demanding too high a price.

clue.text: Mate with bishop positioned to take part

indicators.note: to take part means the answer is a part of the following words, sitting across them

explanation.surface: In chess, a checkmate is set up by placing a bishop to capture a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' and 'bishop' suggest chess, but Mate is the definition, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a colleague or friend, a partner.

clue.text: Film about alien, entertaining while making point

indicators.note: entertaining means the film's title holds the next word inside it

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien
as means while, as in 'as I walked'

explanation.surface: A film about an alien is fun while making its point.
explanation.definitionFit: East is a point of the compass, one cardinal direction.

clue.text: Clergyman keeping warnings about end of Christendom in proportion

indicators.note: keeping means the clergyman's word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman

indicators.note: about means the warnings word surrounds the single letter

parts.note: omens are signs warning of the future

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A churchman keeps prophecies about the end of Christianity in perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes the last letter of Christendom; 'about' wraps the warnings word round it, and 'keeping' sets the result inside the clergyman's word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Commensurate means corresponding in size or degree, proportionate.

clue.text: For score, very short attack

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: In a musical score, a very brief burst of sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For score' says the definition is a musical marking: assai means very in Italian tempo terms, as in allegro assai.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical direction meaning extremely, used in scores.

clue.text: Golf star seen to be playing for glory

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to be playing means the letters are moving about into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A golf star is seen on the course playing for glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf' is the NATO alphabet's word for G, not the sport; 'to be playing' scrambles the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatness is eminence or distinction, a kind of fame.

clue.text: Thus keeping in good spirits about work

indicators.note: about tells us the assembled letters are turned round to read the other way
keeping means the word for thus holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
someone in good spirits is up, cheerful

explanation.surface: A cheerful person is feeling upbeat about their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in good spirits' sits inside 'Thus' via 'keeping', then 'about' turns the whole run backwards to give the musical term for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, a creative product.

clue.text: Cause page to go on waterway carrying message

indicators.note: in a down clue, to go on means to sit above the next piece
carrying means the waterway word holds the message word inside it

parts.note: a river is a natural waterway
a memo is a short written message

explanation.surface: The reason a messenger boy had to travel by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' looks like a servant boy, but it is just its abbreviation; 'carrying' sets the message inside the waterway, and 'to go on' stacks the page letter above in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime mover is the force that sets something going, an originator.

clue.text: Singular little article put together with skill is dear

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
wee is Scottish for little
the is the definite article
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A unique small item, crafted with skill, is precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetheart is a term of endearment, like darling.

clue.text: Expert design of stamp 26 with flower

indicators.note: a design of the letters is a fresh arrangement of them

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A skilled philatelic artist produces a stamp decorated with a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design of' signals a rearrangement of the word stamp; the '26' printed in the clue gives no letters and reads as a scanning slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is someone thoroughly skilled at an activity, an adept.

clue.text: Arouse loud rage

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Provoking someone produces a noisy fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to stir or inflame their feelings, a synonym of arouse.

clue.text: Bishop left upset over toil involved in plan

indicators.note: in means the middle pieces go inside the word for plan

parts.note: to mean is to plan or intend

indicators.note: over means the first piece sits above the second in a down clue
in a down clue, upset means the word reads upwards, turned round

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: involved suggests letters twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A bishop is annoyed about work being part of the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the nautical word for left upwards, 'involved' scrambles toil, 'over' stacks one above the other, and 'in' puts both inside the verb for plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolitan is a senior bishop with authority over a church province.

clue.text: Denigration of bridge's 1st beginning with nasty tilt in part

indicators.note: beginning with places the first piece at the front of what follows
the 1st of a word is its opening letter
in means the shuffled letters go inside the word for part

parts.note: an element is a part or component

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of tilt are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bridge player complains of being insulted, with a nasty tilt of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: '1st' takes the opening letter of bridge's; 'nasty' scrambles tilt, which 'in' lodges within the word for part, and 'beginning with' puts the B in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Denigration is the act of disparaging someone, making them seem small and unimportant.

clue.text: Verse shown to be justified

parts.note: indicated means shown or pointed out

explanation.surface: A poem proves its own point.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindicated means cleared of blame, shown to be right.

clue.text: Bad press, inane, concerning a poet

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Poor and foolish newspaper coverage about a writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges PRESS and INANE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenserian describes things relating to Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan writer of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Love shown by saint in midst of corrupt deception

indicators.note: in midst of means the first pieces go into the middle of the word for corrupt

parts.note: impure means corrupt, tainted
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A loving saint appears among corrupt people, which is itself a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is a fraud, pretending to be someone else.

clue.text: Servant, no good, last to handle stress

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: an underling is a subordinate servant

indicators.note: last to picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A useless servant is the final person to deal with pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline something is to emphasise it.

clue.text: Hour around a certain river

indicators.note: around means the abbreviation for hour is turned round

parts.note: a certain one, as in 'a certain person' meaning one person

explanation.surface: Something takes an hour to go round a particular river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the abbreviation for hour back to front; 'a certain' gives one, as in 'a certain man'. The river runs through Switzerland and France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river flowing through Switzerland and France.

clue.text: One who gives name in 2 entry

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the word for entry

parts.note: a door is an entrance, a way in

explanation.surface: A benefactor writes their name in a register entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2' printed in the clue gives no letters and reads as a scanning slip for 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a benefactor who contributes money, blood or organs.

clue.text: Identification rejected by soldier guarding one exit 3

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation is sent back the other way
guarding means the soldier's word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer, a soldier
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A soldier refuses someone's papers while guarding a single exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' sends the abbreviation for identification back the other way; 'guarding' has the engineer soldier surround the letter for one. The stray '3' gives nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave, to vanish from sight.

clue.text: A seat in the Lords

parts.note: read as a place to sit, a padded leather sofa of the type found in clubs; read as a title, an earl who sat in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: A member of the upper house of Parliament takes their place.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament; one earl of that title gave his name to a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a deep buttoned leather sofa, and the Earls of Chesterfield were peers in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Force that is infiltrated by politician on left

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
infiltrated by means the next piece gets inside the abbreviation

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is
MP is a member of parliament

explanation.surface: A coercion by a left-wing politician who has wormed his way in.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act.

clue.text: Support a gamble

parts.note: a bet is a gamble or wager

explanation.surface: Backing a risky wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Meagre list

definitions.meaning: scanty, as in a thin, poor year
a ship's tilt to one side, as a verb to incline

explanation.definitionFit: Lean means thin and sparse, and also to tilt like a listing ship.

clue.text: Follow story (sound only)

indicators.note: sound only says we want a word that is heard the same, not spelt the same

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Keep up with a narrative only through its audio.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them covertly.

clue.text: Weaken, defending position open to question

indicators.note: defending means the word for weaken surrounds and protects the next piece

parts.note: to disable is to weaken or incapacitate
to put is to place or position

explanation.surface: A weakened defensive position is one that can be argued over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputable can be argued against, being doubtful.

clue.text: Don't accept conclusion reached by study after study

indicators.note: after places the final letter behind the second word's synonym

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Refusing to accept a finding that came after study upon study.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'study' gives its last letter Y; the second gives DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to refuse to admit it, rejecting it as untrue.

clue.text: Successfully elected great working PM once

parts.note: well means successfully, as in 'it went well'
a candidate who is elected is in
GT is an abbreviation for great
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A former prime minister was voted in comfortably and worked hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington was a British prime minister in the 1820s and 1830s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington served as British prime minister, a former head of government.
